key_insight: A formally verified checker can certify a polyhedron’s vertex set using mostly cheap combinatorial tests plus membership checks, making certification faster than full informal vertex enumeration.
engineering_relevance: This provides a trustworthy, automation-friendly path for converting H-representations to certified V-representations in verification and computational geometry pipelines.
method: Start from an informally computed candidate list of vertices.
Use a completeness criterion based on an abstract simplicial complex that generalizes triangulations of the normal fan.
Formally verify the certificate in Rocq, with expensive work reduced mainly to polyhedron membership tests.
evidence_signal: The authors report experiments on many benchmark polyhedra, and the extracted Rocq-to-OCaml checker is typically 1.5x to over 5x faster than lrslib reverse-search enumeration.
watch_item: Speed gains depend on having a good candidate vertex list and efficient membership checking; the approach certifies results rather than replacing the initial enumeration step.
paper_title: Formally Certifying the Vertex Set of a Polyhedron Faster than Informal Enumeration
